claim: Measure the foot in cm from the wall at the heel to the tip of the biggest toe, then use the CM size matrix on the product page
exact_words: Stand with your heel against a wall. With a ruler or measuring tape, measure from the wall to the tip of your biggest toe in centimetres. Use our CM size matrix on the product page of the brand you're interested in and add that item to cart.

claim: Sizes vary by style and brand
exact_words: Sizes can vary by style and by brand and getting the right size for you is important to us.

claim: Sizing tends to be standard across brands but varies slightly by style, shape and material
exact_words: Generally sizing tends to be standard across brands, although sizes can vary slightly depending on the style, shape and material of the shoe.

claim: An owned pair's size is a good guide
exact_words: The size of the pair that you already own is a good guide!

claim: Some styles run large or small; noted on product pages when known
exact_words: Certain brands or styles can run a size larger or smaller. We'll include this information on the product page when we have this information available

claim: True Fit recommends from owned footwear, no measuring
exact_words: Simply answer a few questions to get started - No measuring required.

claim: The guide's charts carry a CM column on all four tabs (Men, Women, Kids, Infants); the page does not say whether CM is the foot's length or the shoe's
exact_words: US MEN’S EU UK CM

claim: Australian sizing is the same as US sizing
exact_words: AUSTRALIAN SIZING Is the same as US sizing.

claim: The size selector switches between US, UK, EU and centimetres
exact_words: For ease, you can switch between US, UK, EU sizing, and centimeters, using the "choose size" dropdown above the size selector.

claim: A properly fitting shoe is snug at heel and midfoot with toe room
exact_words: Remembering that a properly fitting shoe should feel snug at the heel and midfoot, with wiggle room around the toes.

claim: The size charts' length column is headed Foot Length (Millimetres)
exact_words: Foot Length (Millimetres)

claim: Measure both feet, heel against a straight edge, length in mm toe tip to heel
exact_words: Place a ruler beside your foot touching the straight edge your heel is also touching, then take the length in millimetres from the tip of your longest toe to your heel.

claim: Note the longer foot
exact_words: Remember to measure both feet, making a note of the longest.

claim: The chart's ruler measurements do not correlate with the Clarks foot gauge
exact_words: *These measurements do not correlate to measuring with a Clarks foot gauge.

claim: Clarks prints both a Clarks EU size and a Standard EU size for adults
exact_words: Clarks UK Size Clarks EU Size Standard EU Size Foot Length (Millimetres)

claim: Width letters: women D standard, E wide, EE extra wide; men G standard, H wide; kids E narrow, F standard, G wide, H extra wide
exact_words: D Standard Fit / E Wide Fit / EE Extra Wide Fit; G Standard Fit / H Wide Fit; E Narrow Fit / F Standard Fit / G Wide Fit / H Extra Wide Fit

claim: Foot gauge readings are their own unit, not millimetres
exact_words: *Please note, foot gauge measurements are exclusive to this method of measuring and are not in standard millimetres (mm).

claim: Enter the larger foot's length and width into the calculator
exact_words: If you found a slight difference between feet, enter the largest length and width measurements.

claim: The calculator takes length 97-281 and width 67-227 (gauge units)
exact_words: Enter a number between 97-281 / Enter a number between 67-227

claim: In-store fitting recommended; at-home gauge as the alternative
exact_words: For the perfect fit, we recommend visiting our in-store experts. But if you can't make it in, try our hassle-free at-home guides
